q: Which British author created the detective Sherlock Holmes?
note: He grew so tired of Holmes that he killed him off at the Reichenbach Falls, then revived him after a public outcry.

q: Who wrote the Harry Potter series of novels?
note: Her publisher used initials rather than her first name in the hope that boys would pick up the book.

q: Which American author wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer under a pen name?
note: Born Samuel Clemens, he took his pen name from a riverboat call meaning water two fathoms deep.

q: Who wrote The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings?
note: He was a professor of Anglo-Saxon at Oxford, and invented the Elvish languages before he invented the stories.

q: Which Danish writer wrote the fairy tales "The Little Mermaid" and "The Ugly Duckling"?
note: A bronze statue of his little mermaid has sat on a rock in Copenhagen harbour since 1913.

q: Which American writer wrote the poem "The Raven"?
note: The bird's single croaked word, "Nevermore", made him famous almost overnight but earned him only about nine dollars.

q: Which English poet wrote the lines beginning "I wandered lonely as a cloud"?
note: The daffodils in the poem were ones his sister Dorothy described first, in her journal.

q: Which reclusive American poet of Amherst, Massachusetts wrote "Because I could not stop for Death"?
note: Fewer than a dozen of her roughly 1,800 poems were published while she was alive.

q: Which American poet wrote "The Road Not Taken" and "Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening"?
note: He read at John F. Kennedy's inauguration, though glare off the snow forced him to recite from memory instead.

q: Which Russian writer, also a practising doctor, wrote the play The Cherry Orchard?
note: He called medicine his lawful wife and literature his mistress.

q: Which American author wrote A Farewell to Arms and The Old Man and the Sea?
note: His stripped-down style, all short declarative sentences, was shaped by his years as a newspaper reporter.

q: Which Canadian author wrote the dystopian novel The Handmaid's Tale?
note: She has said she included nothing in the book that some society had not already done somewhere.

q: Which Italian poet wrote The Divine Comedy?
note: By writing it in Tuscan rather than Latin he did more than anyone to make that dialect into modern Italian.

q: Which of the Brontë sisters wrote Jane Eyre?
note: She published it as Currer Bell, and reviewers spent months arguing about whether the author was a man.

q: Which Irish writer wrote the novel The Picture of Dorian Gray and the play The Importance of Being Earnest?
note: Earnest opened in London in 1895, at the very height of his fame and only weeks before his ruin.

q: Which Nigerian author wrote Things Fall Apart?
note: He took the title from a line in W.B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming".

q: Which poet wrote the 1922 modernist poem "The Waste Land"?
note: Ezra Pound cut the draft roughly in half, and Eliot dedicated the poem to him in gratitude.

q: Which Argentine writer wrote the labyrinthine short-story collections Ficciones and The Aleph?
note: He went blind in middle age, around the same time he was appointed director of Argentina's national library.

q: Which Japanese noblewoman wrote The Tale of Genji, often called the world's first novel?
note: She wrote it around a thousand years ago as a lady-in-waiting at the Heian imperial court.

q: Which American poet wrote "O Captain! My Captain!", an elegy for Abraham Lincoln?
note: He spent his life expanding a single book, Leaves of Grass, through edition after edition.
